newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends wildly mixed, March down sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends wildly mixed, March down sharply.

text.p: March CME lumber futures posted another sharp decline after Tuesday's limit loss while other months ranged mixed on spread action, traders said.
March fell $8.20 per tbf to close at $411.80 while May was only off $0.50 at $380.10 per tbf. Other months finished $3.90 higher to $0.90 lower.

Bear spreading added to selling pressure encouraged by reports of a weak undertone to cash. Wholesalers are offering spruce in the $390 to $405 range compared to the latest Random Lengths quoted of $416, traders said.
Concern was also growing over the Canadian lumber quota.
For the year ending March 31, only slightly above 20 percent of the fourth-quarter quota and about 85 percent of the yearly quota has been used thus far, analysts noted.
"We are not at a pace to exceed the quota -- mills have to sell their allocations to have the same or larger allocation next year," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Chartists added that the market looked technically weak after gapping below a trend line early.
